cases.excerpt: Because the evidence of association with bladder cancer (BC) is limited, we aimed to assess associations with BC risk for intakes of whole grains, refined grains, and dietary fiber. We pooled individual data from 574,726 participants in 13 cohort studies, 3214 of whom developed incident BC.

effect_size.excerpt: We found that higher intake of total whole grain was associated with lower risk of BC (comparing highest with lowest intake tertile: HR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.77, 0.98; HR per 1-SD increment: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.91, 0.99; P for trend: 0.023).

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 0.73 (95% CI: 0.52–1.01), indicating no statistically significant association between whole-grain intake and bladder cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 75.24%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
